To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SKO 208 was found to be good general combiner and SKO 208 SKO 210 SKO 211, and SKO 212 were found to be good specific combiners for forage yield as well as its contributing traits.

the F2 population of a 10x 10 diallel cross of oats (Avena Sativa) was developed and evaluated for forage yield, days to 50 per cent flowering, plant height, culm diameter at 30 cm, flag leaf length and breadth, number of leaves, seed length, breadth, 1000 seed weight and seed yield, crude protein content and ash content of leaf and seed.

, the estimates of additive genetic variances and dominance variances revealed that magnitude of the former was higher than the latter for forage yield as well as its attributing traits except for days to flowering, culm height and flag leaf length, suggesting the importance of additive gene effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic variability in F2 generation of dially crosses of oats for green fodder yield as well as its attributing traits.
the genetic analysis of forage yield and attributing traits in a set of F2 segregants of diallel mating in oats.
the development of oat cultivars for forage use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SKO 208 was found to be the most suitable parent for the development of improved cultivars for green fodder yield as well as seed yield and its attributive traits.
, SKO 208 was the most promising line for forage yield.
SKO 201, SKO 208 SKO 210 and SKO 212 are best suited as parents for further improvement of forage oats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the F2s derived through the diallel mating scheme were found to be a rich source of variation for the traits studied, and the crosses derived through the diall mating scheme could be exploited in the future breeding programme to produce superior genotypes.
the genetic improvement of the forage yield and contributing traits is possible by the selection of the best parents and the progenies.
SKO 208 is a good choice as general combiner for green fodder yield as well as its attributing traits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of oats as a forage crop can be a viable option for the farmers of Jammu and Kashmir.
the genetic improvement of forage oat cultivars can be achieved through selection based on the GCA effects of the parents.
the F2s derived from crosses involving SKO 208 as one of the parents were found to be good general combiners for green forage yield and seed yield attributing traits.
